depth_findings.text: The HTTP route and JSON shape of model-gateway's GetModelAccess for the BFF (POST /v1/models/access) is not specified by any slice; S4 must serve exactly what the guard sends and reads, or the guard fails closed for every ZDR org restricting PUT.

The guard takes attested model ids from GET /v1/models as the acting admin, which S4 filters by that admin's own stored policy. A model the admin currently cannot see but the draft would allow is not counted as attested, so the guard can refuse a legitimate ZDR policy (the safe direction). It needs an unfiltered attested set, for example an attested flag on ModelAccessEntry.

The guard sends min_privacy_tier as org-core's lower-case label (global, eu_resident, zdr_contractual, sovereign), but the proto field is the PrivacyTier enum. S4's JSON-to-proto mapping must accept the labels.

The guard makes one sequential model-gateway call per restricting layer (up to 21) with a 25 s client ceiling each. There is no concurrency and no latency test; join them if a ZDR org with many role overrides is slow.

The BFF does not check semantic validity (unknown effort, tier, glob, default against policy). org-core answers invalid_model_policy and the guard has already spent a catalogue read by then. Not tested against the real org-core.

Every restricting PUT now reads the org from org-core to learn its ZDR posture, including a failed read that blocks non-ZDR orgs with 503 when org-core is degraded. A stronger fix is for GET policy and PUT to take the posture from the session or from org-core's PUT response.
While the admin switch is on, a policy that would leave the acting admin themself unable to see any model gets no warning; the plan has no self-lockout rule.

Needs the gateway image rebuilt (verevon-gateway-rs), a real org-core with the S2 migration, and real cookies. Not run: the wiremock suite proves the contract shape, not the real org-core delegation signature for the model-entitlement routes.

The pre-existing action-surface-contract.test.mjs fails at HEAD on 11 registry ids with no quoted literal in handlers.rs (approvals.decide, audit.*, chat.answer_question and others), so the plan's `pnpm test` command is red for reasons outside this slice.

The model-gateway route and JSON shape that the guard calls (POST /v1/models/access with {draft, include_catalogue:true}, reading catalogue[{id, entitled}]) is named by no slice. WS10-S4 must serve exactly this, or the guard fails closed for every ZDR org on a restricting PUT.

The guard takes attested model ids from GET /v1/models called as the acting admin. S4 filters that list by the admin's stored policy, so an attested model the admin currently cannot see but the draft would allow is not counted. The guard can then wrongly refuse a legitimate ZDR policy. This is the safe direction, but it needs an unfiltered attested set, for example an attested flag on ModelAccessEntry.

The guard sends min_privacy_tier as org-core's lower-case label, while the proto field is the PrivacyTier enum. S4's JSON-to-proto mapping must accept the labels, or a restricting tier in the draft fails or is misjudged.

zdr_switch_gate judges only what the acting admin sees. If ZDR is turned on after a role policy has been saved, a role whose policy leaves no attested model passes the switch gate whenever the admin still sees one. That role's members are then refused at run time (the safe direction, but silent). The plan has no later role-by-role check at switch time.

The write guard makes one sequential model-gateway call per restricting layer, up to 21, each with a 25 s client ceiling, and there is no latency or concurrency test. Join them if a ZDR org with many role overrides is slow.

The BFF checks structure only, so org-core's semantic invalid_model_policy comes after the guard has already spent a catalogue read and verdict calls. Nothing was tested against a real org-core, including the delegation signature on the model-entitlement routes.

Every restricting PUT reads the org from org-core to learn its ZDR posture, so a degraded org-core blocks even non-ZDR orgs with 503 model_policy_guard_unavailable. Take the posture from the session or from org-core's PUT response instead.
While the admin switch is on, a policy that leaves the acting admin themself with no visible model gets no warning. The plan has no self-lockout rule.
The GET policy route returns 403 to a non-admin member once the switch is on, and `{enabled:false}` to every member while it is off. S6's SPA section must treat 403 as hidden rather than as an error.
Log texts in settings.rs changed from "org ZDR gate" to "org ZDR check" for the credential-mint and catalogue-read failures. Check that no log alert or test greps the old text.

results.notes:
The slice's code and unit tests are built; the admin switch is off by default. With it off: GET model-entitlement answers {enabled:false}, PUT and explain are 404, nothing is called upstream, and the ZDR switch gate does not read hidden_count. The feature is not usable end to end. The ZDR write guard calls POST {model_gateway_url}/v1/models/access, which model-gateway does not serve (WS10-S4 builds the admission side but never names this HTTP route), so for an org with ZDR on a restricting PUT fails closed with 503 until it exists.

What was built:
- Routes: GET and PUT /api/v1/orgs/{id}/model-entitlement and GET .../explain, in the new orgs/model_entitlement.rs.
- Admin gate: PUT and GET policy go through require_org_admin, then org-core's CallerRole check (its refusal passes through; a test covers the two gates disagreeing). Explain is open to a member for themselves; naming another user needs admin.
- Body validation: structural only, mirroring org-core's limits (500 entries, 128 chars, 20 roles, 16 surfaces, 64 KB, unknown fields refused, expected_revision required). org-core keeps the semantic rules.
- ZDR write guard (D10): only judges a layer that can remove a model. It reads the org's ZDR from org-core, then the catalogue, then one draft verdict per restricting layer. A role override replaces the default, so each layer is judged alone. 409 model_policy_leaves_no_zdr_model; any unreadable answer is 503 model_policy_guard_unavailable and never a pass. A body that restricts nothing reads nothing.
- zdr_switch_gate in settings.rs: when the admin switch is on and the catalogue shows no attested model but entitlement.hidden_count > 0, it answers 409 zdr_models_not_entitled. I extracted mint_model_plane_credentials and read_model_catalogue from it and made model_attests_zdr_for_chat pub(super); behaviour is unchanged otherwise, and the log texts for the failed mint and failed catalogue read changed ("org ZDR gate" became "org ZDR check").
- Config: AppState.model_entitlement_admin_enabled, parsed once in build_state, on only for the exact word "true". A test asserts no handler reads the env.
- Action: org.set_model_entitlement (control, risk high, requiresApproval, strict zod schema). It is not in MODEL_EXECUTABLE_ACTION_IDS, and a registry test asserts that. The dispatcher calls the real PUT handler, so the same guard applies; a test asserts it.
- SPA client model-entitlement-client.ts (+ test) and endpoint-map rows.

results.notes: Built: model_access::admit asks inference-core GetModelAccess with the caller's own credential on unary /v1/invoke, SSE /v1/invoke/stream, and gRPC invoke and invoke_stream, before any session-core call. A refusal gives typed 403 or 503, a single SSE error frame, or PERMISSION_DENIED or UNAVAILABLE with trailers; the ZDR branch is under the same admission. It applies only when the answer says enforced. An unnamed model uses the policy's chat default, and that default is itself judged. The effort clamp rewrites req.effort to the policy max_effort with mp_contracts Policy::clamp_effort, mapping the client profile onto the ladder and back to the legacy quick/deep when the ladder is off, and it can only lower a request. list_models adds an optional entitlement sibling field, left out when no policy is applied. New trailers are mapped in grpc_status_to_http (503 for unavailable), invoke_inference_error, the ZDR direct stream arm and the durable fallback error frame. get_policy fills allowed_models from GetModelAccess with include_catalogue. set_policy still refuses by name, now pointing at PUT /api/v1/orgs/{id}/model-entitlement. No new switch: it follows GetModelAccess.enforced, so with MODEL_ENTITLEMENT_MODE off nothing changes (the only added cost is one gRPC call per turn). Not done: the execution-core typed run failure itself needs src edits outside my files, so only the contract test exists (status never FAILED_PRECONDITION, not a ZDR refusal, not in the subscription reader's closed code list, content-free, inference-core uses the catalogue builders).
